clue.text: Food concepts that go beyond the amateur?

parts.note: someone who has gone past amateur status is a pro, a professional
visions are ideas or concepts of what might be

explanation.surface: A question about ideas that rise above amateur level, perhaps a chef's ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split: ideas beyond amateur level are 'pro visions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Provisions are supplies of food and drink laid in for later use.

clue.text: Revolutionary outbreak sees school place taking precedence

indicators.note: the word for place goes first, ahead of the school abbreviation

parts.note: to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: A school sees an uprising break out while one location pushes to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden violent attempt to seize power, a coup or uprising.

clue.text: Young fliers terribly slow to welcome jets without wings

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the shuffled word holds the other piece inside it
terribly suggests the letters of slow are badly mangled and rearranged
wings are the outer edges, so jets loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Baby birds are painfully slow next to wingless jet aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without wings' trims the outer letters; 'terribly' gives OWLS, and 'to welcome' makes it take in the trimmed piece before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Owlets are baby owls, and birds are fliers, so young owls are young fliers.

clue.text: Rancour working in support of royal capacity

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath, so the royal word comes first above

parts.note: imperial means belonging to an emperor or empire, close to royal
gall is bitterness or rancour
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Bitterness is at work in backing the monarchy's role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal capacity' reads as a monarch's role; 'capacity' alone is the definition, a measure of volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperial gallon is a British unit of liquid volume, and capacity means volume held.

clue.text: Question one aspect under adjustment of rent

indicators.note: in a down clue the view piece lies beneath the reshuffled rent

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

indicators.note: an adjustment rearranges, so the letters of rent are reshuffled

parts.note: a view is an outlook or aspect

explanation.surface: A tenant queries one feature of a rent review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustment of' shuffles the rent letters; 'under' works because this is a down clue, so the aspect word sits below them.
explanation.definitionFit: To interview someone is to question them formally, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Trouble in the outskirts of Nantes resulting in arrests

indicators.note: in places the trouble word inside the two letters picked from the city name
outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of Nantes

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Unrest on the edge of the French city of Nantes leads to police arrests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outskirts of' gives N and S from Nantes, with AIL put between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a suspect is informal for catching or arresting them.

clue.text: Pack abandoning wife for quiet break

indicators.note: abandoning the wife letter for another means swapping it out for the quiet letter

parts.note: to stow luggage is to pack it
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A man leaves his wife and packs his bags for a peaceful getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning wife for quiet' replaces the W in STOW with P.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is a pause or halt in a journey, which is a break.

clue.text: Work of art needing expedition on credit reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a trip is an expedition and tick is British slang for credit; in a down clue trip sits on tick

explanation.surface: A painting is acquired for a journey paid for on account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on credit' uses TICK, British slang for buying on credit; TRIP TICK spoken matches the art term.
explanation.definitionFit: A triptych is a painting or carving on three hinged panels, often an altarpiece.

clue.text: New Age Spain convert?

indicators.note: new shows the letters of Age Spain are made into something fresh by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Is Spain being won over by New Age spirituality?
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age' looks like one phrase, but 'New' is the anagram signal working on AGE SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To paganise is to turn people to heathen belief, a kind of religious conversion.

clue.text: How sanctimonious setter might be compared to you!

definitions.text: How sanctimonious setter might be compared to you!

parts.words: How sanctimonious setter might be compared to you!
parts.note: a smug setter would claim to be more saintly than the solver, using the old familiar word for you

explanation.surface: A setter preens about being better than the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: Thou is the archaic form of you; the phrase is what the self-righteous setter would say of the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a smugly self-righteous attitude of moral superiority over others.

clue.text: Flower cult essentially adopted by crown

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the middle letters go inside the crown word

parts.note: the crown of something is its top or tip

indicators.note: the essence is the heart, so take the middle letters of cult

explanation.surface: A cult of flower worship is taken up by the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crown' suggests royalty but means the top of something; 'essentially' and 'adopted by' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a spring bulb bloom, a well-known example of a garden flower.

clue.text: Cutting business for profit

parts.note: a tailor makes a living from cutting cloth to make clothes, a commercial cutting trade

explanation.surface: A firm slashes costs or jobs to boost its profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' suggests corporate cutbacks; the trade meant is cutting cloth for paying customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailoring is the craft and trade of cutting and sewing made-to-measure clothes.

clue.text: Nurse must stock them occasionally for supplier

indicators.note: to stock is to hold inside, so the carer word contains the picked letters

parts.note: to nurse someone is to look after them, which a carer does

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so take every other letter of them

explanation.surface: A nurse is told to keep a supply of something on hand now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' picks T and E from THEM, which go inside CARER.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer provides food and drink for events, so is a supplier of meals.

clue.text: Offspring must eat lean dairy product

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the offspring word holds the lean word

parts.note: a son is a male offspring
to lean is to tilt

explanation.surface: A child is told to eat lean food from the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lean' looks like an adjective for meat but is the verb, TILT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a strong blue English cheese, and cheese is a dairy product.

clue.text: Compensating factors of money set aside during thanksgiving? The other way round!

indicators.note: during would put the savings word inside the other, but the clue then reverses that
the reversal phrase swaps container and contents, so the thanksgiving word goes inside the money word

parts.note: savings are money put by
grace is a short prayer of thanks before a meal

explanation.surface: Money saved over the Thanksgiving holiday, or rather the reverse, offsets something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'during' puts the money inside the prayer; 'The other way round!' tells you to swap container and contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving graces are redeeming qualities that make up for someone's or something's faults.

clue.text: US conscript must pack a coarse biscuit

indicators.note: packing means holding inside, so the soldier letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: GI is the term for an American soldier
ribald means crude or coarse

explanation.surface: An American soldier stows a rough army biscuit in his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: A GARIBALDI is a British biscuit with a layer of currants pressed between thin pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garibaldi is a currant biscuit named after the Italian general, a type of biscuit.

clue.text: Nation may be secure after cost is worked out

indicators.note: the secure word comes after the reworked cost
worked out means solved or reorganised, so the letters of cost are rearranged

parts.note: to land something, like a deal, is to secure it

explanation.surface: A country might be safe once its budget is calculated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is worked out' signals the shuffle (giving SCOT); 'may be secure' hides the verb land, as in landing a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland is a nation, one of the four countries of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Lack of vitality is not so much about one elected member (northern)

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for not so much goes round the rest

parts.note: something that is not so much is less
the Roman numeral I is one
an MP is an elected Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A tired northern MP is described as having less energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you the comparative phrase goes round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpness is floppiness or lack of firmness, so a want of energy or vigour.

clue.text: Cold call English luminary — how embarrassing!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to ring someone is to call them on the phone
a worthy is an eminent person, a luminary

explanation.surface: Cold-calling a famous English figure turns out mortifying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold call' reads as one phrase but splits into C and RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cringeworthy makes you squirm with awkwardness, so it is mortifying.

clue.text: You're texting about certain person of interest?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the text-speak letters surround the certain word

parts.note: in text messages you're is shortened to UR
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A detective texts someone, asking whether they are sure about a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'person of interest' is police jargon for a suspect; here it means someone who charges interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at excessive rates, someone whose trade is charging interest.

clue.text: Places of learning once available to all

parts.note: unis is short for universities, places of learning
ex means former, once

explanation.surface: Universities were once open to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Unisex describes clothing or facilities suitable for either sex, open to everyone.

clue.text: Hints about line crossed during exercise drinks

indicators.note: about means going round, so the hints word encloses the rest

parts.note: tips are hints or helpful suggestions

indicators.note: the line is set down across the middle of the exercise letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Advice about crossing a line during a workout, delivered with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'crossed during' sets the line in the exercise, and 'about' wraps the hints round that.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipples are alcoholic drinks, as in a favourite tipple.

clue.text: Team covering left edge

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the team word goes over the left letter

parts.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A football team protects its left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edge' looks like a noun for the wing but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to edge along furtively or sideways, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Blessing meat after change of starter

indicators.note: the starter is the first letter, which gets swapped for a different one

parts.note: venison is deer meat

explanation.surface: Grace is said over the meat once the first course has been changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' suggests a first course but means the first letter: V becomes B.
explanation.definitionFit: A benison is an old literary word for a blessing or benediction.

clue.text: No idea about boy returning with voice so affected

indicators.note: about can mean in a jumble, so the letters of no idea are rearranged
returning means going back, so the boy word is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy comes home with a strange voice and no idea why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NO IDEA into ADENOI; 'returning' makes LAD into DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An adenoidal voice sounds nasal, as if from swollen adenoids blocking the nose.

clue.text: Instruments that may be pointed when cycling?

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from one end to the other, here the front one to the back

parts.note: something sharp is pointed

explanation.surface: Musical instruments are asked whether they can be sharp-tipped on a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' moves the S of SHARP to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Harps are stringed musical instruments plucked with the fingers.

clue.text: Touch and run

definitions.meaning: a touch is a small amount

explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a tiny quantity, a touch, and dashing is hurrying, running.

clue.text: Drama created by inspector in new exposure

indicators.note: in places the inspector letters inside the rearranged word
new means made afresh, so the letters of exposure are rearranged

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective's new revelation produces a dramatic story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal and 'in' puts the inspector inside; 'created by' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus Rex is Sophocles' Greek tragedy, a classic stage drama.
